title: Noise, Interference and the Limits of Detection

contract.reader: An engineer or student building a sensor channel, with basic circuits and statistics, who wants to know what limits the smallest change the channel can resolve
contract.problem: Telling noise from interference, estimating each noise source, combining them, and knowing which remedy acts on which problem
contract.outcome: Compute thermal, shot and 1/f noise and a filter's noise bandwidth; choose an amplifier for a source resistance; use averaging and dither within their limits; recognize the four interference coupling paths and their remedies; build a noise budget and state effective resolution, noise-free resolution and a detection limit
contract.contribution: The series' load-cell channel (and the photodiode of entry 2) carried from noise physics to a complete noise budget, every number derived on the page and tied back to the converter choice of the previous entry
contract.evidence: Derivations and worked numbers on the page; Horowitz and Hill (2015); Motchenbacher and Connelly (1993); Ott (2009); Pallas-Areny and Webster (2001)
contract.limitations: White, shot and 1/f noise only; interference treated with order-of-magnitude examples; no measurement procedure for the budget

findings.location: Section 2.2, inline shot-noise expression sqrt(2 x 1.602e-19 x 0.55e-6) (360 px)
findings.problem: The page scrolls sideways at 360 px (page width 364 px); the only element wider than the viewport is this inline KaTeX square root, which cannot break and is cut at the right edge
findings.whyItMatters: On a phone the whole page shifts sideways under the thumb and the end of the expression is hidden
findings.action: Move the expression to a display equation or split it into steps so no inline expression exceeds about 300 px
findings.acceptance: New captures show horizontalScroll false at 360 px and the shot-noise sentence fully visible

findings.location: Section 4, paragraph 'The dither must be large enough', last sentences
findings.problem: 'Nearly five bits of resolution gained' compares the averaged RMS error q/28 with one step q; against the q/sqrt(12) RMS of a single quantized reading (the page's own effective-resolution measure, Section 6.1) the gain is about three bits
findings.whyItMatters: A reader applying the page's definition gets three bits, not five, and may doubt the arithmetic or the definition
findings.action: State the baseline of the gain, or express it in the terms of Section 6.1
findings.acceptance: The sentence names what the gain is measured against and the figure agrees with that baseline

findings.location: Section 2.3, underbraced display equation for the 0.1 to 10 Hz band (360 px)
findings.problem: The white-noise term and its value 31.5 nV are hidden behind an unmarked sideways scroll; the next sentence gives the 74.8 nV total that depends on it
findings.whyItMatters: A phone reader sees one of the two terms of the reported sum at the point it is used
findings.action: Stack the two underbraced terms, one per line (gathered block)
findings.acceptance: At 360 px both terms and both values are visible without sideways scrolling
